task_description: Predicting the adsorption energy of lithium polysulfides (Li2S) on diatomic site catalysts (DASCs) to identify key electronic and structural features governing the ensemble effect—i.e., inter-site communication and coordination structure effects among multiple active sites—in sulfur electrochemical reactions for Li||S batteries.

datasets.db_title: DFT-calculated adsorption energies of Li2S on diatomic site catalysts
datasets.db_description: A custom computational dataset containing adsorption energies of Li2S on 21 distinct diatomic site catalysts (DASCs), including Fe-based pairs (e.g., FeCo, FeNi, FeCu) and homonuclear pairs (e.g., ScSc, TiTi, VV), computed via spin-polarized DFT using VASP with PBE+D3 functional. The dataset serves as the target label (regression output) for training and evaluating the interpretable multi-view machine learning framework to uncover physicochemical descriptors—such as corrected d-band centers, electronegativity, atomic radii, and N–M bond lengths—that govern the ensemble effect in multi-site electrocatalysis.

A hand-engineered, domain-informed feature dataset comprising 182 potential descriptors for 21 DASCs, categorized into component features (e.g., electronegativity χM, first ionization energy I1M1, d-band center εd_M, d-electron count θM), site & structure features (e.g., metal–metal distance, N–M bond lengths L3N, atomic radii RM1/RM, bond angles θM1-M), and reference features (e.g., composite terms like (RM1 + RM) × θM). This dataset was constructed from DFT inputs and chemical intuition, then filtered and refined via correlation analysis, wrapper selection, and XGBoost embedding to identify the minimal predictive subspace for Li2S adsorption energy—directly supporting the task of decoding the ensemble effect.
